definition: A persistent service that every participant in a multi-agent system relies on for shared rules about who may take part and with which permissions, how each act is recorded against whoever made it, and how money moves when work is settled.
The crashed or abandoned session whose work a successor session continues, named in the successor's first note.
A joint distribution of private recommendations from a mediator such that every player, knowing only its own recommendation, prefers to follow it.
A session's sequence of timestamped notes recording its observations, decisions and progress, to which notes can be added but never changed.
One append-only Merkle log per harbor, in the style of Certificate Transparency, whose leaves are the roots of completed sessions and whose state the daemon signs as checkpoints.
The daemon's signature over a harbor log's current size and root; Certificate Transparency calls it a signed tree head.
The short list of sibling hashes, with a signed root, that lets anyone check that one note belongs to a recorded session.
The short list of hashes showing that a larger signed checkpoint of an append-only log extends a smaller one, with every earlier entry kept unchanged.
Sen's condition that at least two individuals each have a pair of outcomes over which their own preference decides the social choice.
The graph whose vertices are active sessions and whose edges join sessions that hold overlapping file claims.
Collateral, a fixed fraction of the disputed amount, that an agent posts to challenge a settlement and forfeits if the appeal fails.
The queue of agents declared dead whose work is waiting for a successor.
What a successor receives when it takes over a dead agent's work: the task's purpose, the evidence trail and the file claims.
The assumption that, before each round of a repeated game, every player sees the same correct record of all past actions.
A repeated-game strategy that punishes a deviation for a fixed number of rounds and then returns to cooperation.
The human and compute cost of detecting, assessing and recovering from one breach.
An agent that proposes bond sizes for other agents' work and is itself bonded on the accuracy of its proposals.
The most that will be paid out on a claim under a bond or an insurer's quote.
A coordination act whose effect is to tell other participants something, such as a signal, a request or a proposal.
The total of a project's wallet, escrow and commons-pool balances, which only a top-up can change.
An outside party that absorbs or collects the difference so that a team's own transfers need not balance.
